name: Amazon Athena
definition: Query data in S3 and supported sources with serverless SQL.
example: Find error records in logs stored as Parquet.

name: Amazon EMR
definition: Run managed big-data frameworks such as Apache Spark and Hadoop.
example: Transform a large data lake dataset.

name: AWS Glue
definition: Discover, catalog, and transform data with managed integration tools.
example: Run ETL jobs and publish tables to the Glue Data Catalog.

name: Amazon Kinesis (Data Streams)
definition: Capture and retain ordered streams of records for multiple consumers.
example: Process application events as they arrive.

name: Amazon OpenSearch Service
definition: Run managed OpenSearch clusters or serverless collections for search and analytics.
example: Search application logs and visualize operational trends.

name: Amazon Quick (now AWS Quick)
definition: Use an AI workspace to analyze data and work with connected information. AWS Quick Sight provides its business intelligence and dashboard capabilities.
example: Use Quick Sight to visualize monthly sales from a connected data source.

name: Amazon Redshift
definition: Run SQL analytics in a managed data warehouse.
example: Join large sales and customer tables for reporting.

name: Amazon EventBridge
definition: Route events from supported sources to targets using rules on an event bus.
example: Send order-created events to selected processing services.

name: Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS)
definition: Publish messages to subscribers using topics and supported delivery protocols.
example: Fan out one notification to several endpoints.

name: Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS)
definition: Buffer messages in managed queues for asynchronous processing.
example: Absorb spikes so workers can catch up at their own pace.

name: AWS Step Functions
definition: Orchestrate tasks with a state machine, including branching, retries, and errors.
example: Coordinate document processing across Lambda and other services.

name: Amazon Connect
definition: Operate a cloud contact center with routing, agent tools, and analytics.
example: Route incoming customer calls to available agents.

name: Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES)
definition: Send or receive email through a managed email delivery service.
example: Send transactional password reset messages.

name: AWS Budgets
definition: Set cost, usage, or commitment budgets and receive threshold alerts.
example: Notify an owner when projected spending exceeds a target.

name: AWS Cost and Usage Reports
definition: Export granular AWS cost and usage line items for analysis.
example: Build chargeback reports from detailed billing data.

name: AWS Cost Explorer
definition: Analyze historical AWS cost and usage and view forecasts.
example: Compare monthly spend by service or account.

name: AWS Marketplace
definition: Discover and procure software, data, and services from participating sellers.
example: Purchase a commercial AMI or SaaS subscription.

name: AWS Batch
definition: Queue, schedule, and run batch jobs on managed compute capacity.
example: Process thousands of simulations in parallel.

name: Amazon EC2
definition: Rent virtual servers with configurable instance types, networking, and storage.
example: Run an application when you need control of the guest OS.

name: AWS Elastic Beanstalk
definition: Deploy application code while AWS provisions common infrastructure such as EC2 and a load balancer.
example: Launch a conventional web app while retaining infrastructure access.

name: Amazon Lightsail
definition: Bundle virtual servers, networking, and optional managed databases with simplified pricing.
example: Host a small WordPress site without assembling a large AWS stack.

name: AWS Outposts
definition: Install AWS-managed infrastructure on premises and connect it to a parent AWS Region.
example: Run supported services close to a factory with local latency needs.

name: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR)
definition: Store, scan, and distribute container images.
example: Publish a private Docker image for deployment to ECS.

name: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS)
definition: Run and manage containers using AWS-native orchestration.
example: Host a containerized API on EC2 or Fargate.

name: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
definition: Run Kubernetes with an AWS-managed control plane.
example: Move an existing Kubernetes application onto AWS.

name: AWS Support
definition: Provide account assistance and optional technical support plans.
example: Open a technical case according to your plan’s entitlements.

name: Amazon Aurora
definition: Use an AWS-built relational database compatible with MySQL or PostgreSQL.
example: Run transactional workloads with replicated database storage.

name: Amazon DocumentDB
definition: Use a managed document database compatible with supported MongoDB workloads.
example: Store flexible JSON-like application records.

name: Amazon DynamoDB
definition: Store and retrieve key-value and document data in a serverless NoSQL database.
example: Track shopping carts using a partition key.

name: Amazon ElastiCache
definition: Run managed Valkey, Redis OSS, or Memcached caching.
example: Reduce backing database reads by caching frequently requested results.

name: Amazon Neptune
definition: Store and query graphs using supported graph models and APIs.
example: Explore relationships among devices, accounts, and transactions.

name: Amazon RDS
definition: Operate managed relational engines with built-in backup and maintenance options.
example: Run a PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server, or Db2 database.

name: AWS CLI (Command Line Interface)
definition: Call AWS operations from a command line or scripts.
example: List resources across accounts using configured profiles.

name: AWS CodeBuild
definition: Run managed build and test jobs using a configured environment.
example: Build and test an application on a proposed code change.

name: AWS CodePipeline
definition: Model and automate source, build, test, and deployment stages.
example: Run the release process whenever approved code changes.

name: AWS X-Ray
definition: Trace requests across distributed applications and surface delays or errors.
example: Find which downstream service slows an API request.

name: Amazon AppStream 2.0 (now Amazon WorkSpaces Applications)
definition: Stream desktops or individual applications to users without installing them locally.
example: Deliver a Windows application through a browser.

name: Amazon WorkSpaces
definition: Deliver managed virtual desktops so users can access their work environment from supported devices.
example: Give remote employees access to centrally managed Windows desktops.

name: Amazon WorkSpaces Secure Browser
definition: Deliver a managed remote browser session isolated from the user device.
example: Let workforce users access restricted internal web applications.

name: AWS Amplify
definition: Build and host full-stack web applications using managed deployment tooling.
example: Deploy a frontend from a Git repository.

name: AWS IoT Core
definition: Authenticate devices and exchange messages with cloud applications using supported protocols.
example: Send MQTT telemetry from sensors to a cloud data pipeline.

name: Amazon Comprehend
definition: Analyze text for entities, sentiment, language, and other features.
example: Identify themes in customer comments.

name: Amazon Lex
definition: Build voice or text conversational interfaces using intents and slots.
example: Create a booking bot that collects a date and location.

name: Amazon Polly
definition: Turn written text into synthesized speech.
example: Read a notification aloud in an application.

name: Amazon Q
definition: Use generative AI assistants for tasks such as software development and working with AWS resources. Amazon Q Developer can answer AWS questions and explain code.
example: Ask Amazon Q Developer to explain an unfamiliar function or an AWS service.

name: Amazon Rekognition
definition: Analyze images and videos for supported labels and other visual features.
example: Tag a library of images by detected objects.

name: Amazon SageMaker AI
definition: Develop, train, and deploy machine learning models on managed infrastructure.
example: Train a custom model and serve predictions from an endpoint.

name: Amazon Textract
definition: Extract printed text and structured information from documents and images.
example: Capture fields and tables from a scanned invoice.

name: Amazon Transcribe
definition: Convert spoken audio to text in batch or streaming workflows.
example: Produce a searchable transcript of a recorded meeting.

name: Amazon Translate
definition: Translate text between supported languages.
example: Produce multilingual versions of a product description.

name: AWS Auto Scaling
definition: Coordinate scaling plans for supported AWS resources.
example: Set scaling targets across multiple eligible resource types.

name: AWS CloudFormation
definition: Provision related AWS resources as stacks from declarative templates.
example: Recreate a network environment from a reviewed template.

name: AWS CloudTrail
definition: Record supported account and API activity for audit and investigation.
example: Determine which principal changed a configuration.

name: Amazon CloudWatch
definition: Collect metrics, alarms, logs, and other observability signals.
example: Send an alert when service errors exceed a threshold.

name: AWS Compute Optimizer
definition: Analyze usage and recommend more suitable resource configurations.
example: Identify EC2 instances sized larger than measured usage requires.

name: AWS Config
definition: Track supported resource configuration and evaluate rules against it.
example: Identify buckets that drift from approved settings.

name: AWS Control Tower
definition: Set up and govern a multi-account AWS landing zone.
example: Provision accounts with common guardrails.

name: AWS Health Dashboard
definition: Show AWS service status and events affecting customer resources.
example: Investigate whether an AWS service event affects your account.

name: AWS License Manager
definition: Track software license usage and enforce selected license rules.
example: Monitor deployment of bring-your-own-license workloads.

name: AWS Management Console
definition: Use a browser-based interface for AWS services.
example: Inspect a resource without writing a CLI command.

name: AWS Organizations
definition: Centralize account grouping, consolidated billing, and organization policies.
example: Apply an SCP to an organizational unit.

name: AWS Service Catalog
definition: Publish approved products and control how users provision them.
example: Let teams launch a reviewed infrastructure template.

name: Service Quotas
definition: View and request increases for supported AWS quotas.
example: Check regional capacity limits before a rollout.

name: AWS Systems Manager
definition: Operate managed nodes and cloud resources using centralized tools and automation.
example: Inventory hosts and apply scheduled patches.

name: AWS Trusted Advisor
definition: Provide AWS recommendations across supported best-practice categories.
example: Identify possible idle resources or configuration concerns.

name: AWS Well-Architected Tool
definition: Review architecture decisions against AWS Well-Architected guidance.
example: Record improvement opportunities during an architecture review.

name: AWS Application Discovery Service
definition: Collect server inventory and dependency information in supported environments.
example: Understand which servers should move together before scheduling a migration.

name: AWS Application Migration Service
definition: Replicate compatible servers for lift-and-shift migration to AWS.
example: Move an existing VM while minimizing changes to its application.

name: AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS)
definition: Move data between supported databases with optional ongoing change replication.
example: Replicate a source database during a planned platform migration.

definition: Analyze existing infrastructure and utilization to estimate AWS migration costs and build a business case.
example: Estimate the cost of running a data center’s workloads on AWS before committing to a migration.
name: Migration Evaluator
AWS Migration Hub
definition: Centralize visibility of migration progress from supported tools.
example: View which applications have completed migration.

definition: Assess database compatibility and convert schemas and database code for a move between different database engines.
example: Convert an Oracle schema for use with PostgreSQL before migrating the data.
name: AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT)
Amazon API Gateway
definition: Create, secure, and operate HTTP, REST, or WebSocket API endpoints.
example: Expose a Lambda-backed serverless API.

name: Amazon CloudFront
definition: Deliver content through an edge network with caching and secure origin options.
example: Speed delivery of site assets to geographically distributed users.

name: AWS Direct Connect
definition: Establish a dedicated network connection between a customer location and AWS.
example: Provide predictable private connectivity for a data center.

name: AWS Global Accelerator
definition: Provide fixed entry-point IPs and route supported traffic through the AWS global network.
example: Improve access to regional application endpoints without relying on DNS changes.

name: AWS PrivateLink
definition: Access supported services privately through interface endpoints.
example: Connect to a SaaS provider without sending traffic over a public internet route.

name: Amazon Route 53
definition: Host DNS zones, register domains, and route names according to policies and health.
example: Route requests to a backup endpoint when the primary becomes unhealthy.

name: AWS Transit Gateway
definition: Connect many VPCs and on-premises networks through a regional routing hub.
example: Replace a large mesh of individual VPC peering connections.

name: Amazon VPC
definition: Create logically isolated networks with subnets, routing, and traffic controls.
example: Place public load balancers and private application servers in separate subnets.

definition: Provide encrypted connectivity between AWS and remote networks or users through Site-to-Site VPN and Client VPN.
example: Connect a branch office and give remote employees access to private resources in AWS.
name: AWS VPN
AWS Site-to-Site VPN
definition: Build IPsec tunnels between an external network and AWS.
example: Connect a branch network without provisioning a dedicated circuit.

name: AWS Client VPN
definition: Provide managed remote-user VPN access to AWS and connected networks.
example: Give authorized employees access to private applications.

name: AWS Artifact
definition: Provide access to AWS compliance reports and eligible agreements.
example: Download assurance documentation during an audit.

name: AWS Certificate Manager (ACM)
definition: Provision and manage supported public or private TLS certificates.
example: Attach a managed public certificate to an Application Load Balancer.

name: AWS CloudHSM
definition: Operate dedicated cloud hardware security modules for customer-controlled crypto operations.
example: Use a supported HSM interface for an application with hardware key requirements.

name: Amazon Cognito
definition: Provide customer identity, sign-in, and federated access for applications.
example: Add a signup and login flow to a mobile app.

name: Amazon Detective
definition: Correlate security evidence to help investigate suspicious AWS activity.
example: Trace related principals and events around a finding.

name: AWS Directory Service
definition: Provide managed Microsoft Active Directory options and directory connectivity.
example: Join Windows workloads to a managed domain.

name: AWS Firewall Manager
definition: Administer supported firewall and protection policies across AWS Organizations accounts.
example: Apply a standard web ACL policy to multiple teams.

name: Amazon GuardDuty
definition: Detect suspicious activity using supported cloud and workload telemetry.
example: Investigate a threat finding for unusual account activity.

name: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
definition: Define identities, roles, and permissions for AWS resources.
example: Grant a workload the minimum actions it needs.

name: AWS IAM Identity Center
definition: Manage workforce access to multiple AWS accounts and supported applications.
example: Give a team one sign-in and account-specific permission sets.

name: Amazon Inspector
definition: Assess supported AWS workloads for software vulnerabilities and exposure.
example: Find vulnerable packages in container images.

name: AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS)
definition: Create and control managed encryption keys and cryptographic operations.
example: Set a key policy for encrypting S3 objects.

name: Amazon Macie
definition: Identify sensitive data and security findings in S3.
example: Find objects that may contain personal identifiers.

name: AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM)
definition: Share eligible AWS resources across accounts without transferring ownership.
example: Let multiple accounts use shared subnets.

name: AWS Secrets Manager
definition: Store and retrieve sensitive values with access controls and supported rotation.
example: Deliver database credentials to a workload at runtime.

name: AWS Security Hub
definition: Collect and prioritize security signals across workloads and accounts.
example: See findings from multiple AWS security services in one place.

name: AWS Shield
definition: Protect eligible resources from distributed denial-of-service attacks with Standard and Advanced tiers.
example: Add enhanced DDoS protection for a critical public endpoint.

name: AWS WAF
definition: Inspect web requests and apply application-layer access rules.
example: Block requests that match a managed web attack rule.

name: AWS Fargate
definition: Supply serverless compute capacity for supported ECS tasks and EKS pods.
example: Run containers without managing container hosts.

name: AWS Lambda
definition: Run functions in response to events without provisioning servers.
example: Resize an image when it lands in an S3 bucket.

name: AWS Backup
definition: Centrally set backup schedules, retention, and recovery policies for supported resources.
example: Apply one backup policy to supported databases and volumes.

name: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)
definition: Provide persistent block volumes for EC2 instances.
example: Attach an operating-system or database disk to a VM.

name: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)
definition: Provide shared elastic NFS file storage for supported clients.
example: Give Linux containers concurrent access to shared files.

name: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery
definition: Continuously replicate eligible workloads for recovery on AWS.
example: Fail over on-premises servers during an outage.

name: Amazon FSx
definition: Provide managed file systems including Windows File Server, Lustre, ONTAP, and OpenZFS.
example: Select a file system based on protocol and workload requirements.

name: Amazon S3
definition: Store objects in buckets with API access, storage classes, and lifecycle rules.
example: Store application uploads or build a data lake.

name: Amazon S3 Glacier storage classes
definition: Store infrequently accessed S3 objects at archival storage rates with class-dependent retrieval options.
example: Keep compliance records for long retention periods.

name: AWS Storage Gateway
definition: Connect on-premises environments with AWS storage through file, volume, and tape gateways.
example: Replace a physical backup tape workflow with virtual tapes.
